documentation.title: Coulomb friction: a loaded patch dragged ACROSS A KINK
documentation.description:
A short block, loaded by a real pressure, dragged along a shallow tent and ACROSS ITS APEX, where the contact normal jumps by 2*atan(0.05) = 0.0999 rad. Every point that crosses re-pairs onto a primary element with a different normal while carrying friction.
WHAT IT GUARDS is a setting rather than a feature: tangent="consistent" is REQUIRED here. With the default tangent="reduced" the identical model diverges once the block's leading edge passes the apex. The kink is not the mechanism -- sweeping the tent slope to zero reproduces the same divergence on a flat interface. What fails is the reduced tangent, a fixed-point iteration whose contraction degrades as the total slide grows, where the consistent tangent is Newton and stays flat. This is the COMPLEMENT of ContactFrictionPartialSlip2d, which guards the default because "consistent" fails as soon as any point STICKS; neither dominates.
THE INVARIANT: contactForceY = p*L = 2e5, exactly, by vertical equilibrium. The drive is prescribed in x only, so its reaction carries no vertical load, and the pressure acts on a flat top of length 0.2. Being an equilibrium statement it is insensitive to the pressure distribution, which is the point: on a kinked interface no distribution is predictable. It is exact only quasi-statically, hence T = 9.6 s; the residual is the block's own inertia.
contactForceX is NEGATIVE while the block is driven in +x: the resultant is the traction on the SECONDARY body and friction opposes its motion.
THE KINEMATIC FINGERPRINT: numCells 4 -> 6 and numPoints 8 -> 12, because the block comes to straddle the apex and is cut by one more primary boundary. Both are frozen under slidingType="small", so these integers gate large sliding rather than merely exercising it.
All 8 active points slip, so totalTangentialForce/totalContactForce is mu: the tangent direction flips across the apex, but by at most cos(Dtheta/2) = 0.99875, so the ratio cannot leave [0.39950, 0.40000].
